item.title: Meet Nithya Ravuri, California school student whose nonprofit has grown to more than 500 members
item.description: A California high school senior founded Sevah Neuro, a global network for neurodivergent children. This organization provides resources and social connections, growing to over 500 members worldwide. Sevah Neuro offers a summer fellowship program with life skills and social activities for children. The student-led initiative also engages in legislative advocacy for greater awareness and resources. Future plans include developing an educational book, a mobile app, and physical learning centers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2002, Idaho buried nearly 300 tons of crushed waste glass beneath Highway 75
item.description: Idaho's innovative approach has seen nearly 300 tonnes of waste glass repurposed as road foundation material, addressing both engineering challenges and local waste management issues. The crushed glass cullet, strategically laid beneath a highway section, has proven to be an effective solution, showcasing the potential of recycling in constructing sustainable infrastructure. This project represents a significant advancement in civil engineering practices through resource optimization.

item.title: Messi Retirement Announcement: IShowSpeed reels at Fabrizio Romano post; fans feel end of era
item.description: IShowSpeed was left visibly devastated after learning that Lionel Messi had officially retired from Argentina international football. During a livestream, Speed watched Fabrizio Romano’s announcement and struggled to believe it, repeatedly asking if the transfer journalist was lying. Messi, 39, made the decision after Argentina’s 2026 World Cup final loss to Spain and the death of his father, Jorge, earlier in August. It showed how deeply Messi matters to Speed.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Meet Jonathan Thai, the 17-year-old whose nonprofit raised $30,000, donated 400 bikes
item.description: After a local retailer slashed community biking programs, a Georgia teenager took action by founding Pedal Forward. This initiative has successfully raised over thirty thousand dollars, providing four hundred bicycles to children in need. Hundreds have benefited from free cycling skills clinics, and the organization's reach is expanding into Tennessee and New York. Now, Pedal Forward is setting its sights internationally, planning humanitarian efforts in Vietnam.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 5 popular streamers Ethan Klein has sued in the past 3 years: iDubbbz, Denims and more
item.description: Ethan Klein's legal battles with streamers have taken several turns since 2025. Denims, Kaceytron, Frogan and SeanDaBlack became involved in a copyright dispute surrounding Klein's “Content Nuke: Hasan Piker” video, while iDubbbz faced a separate defamation lawsuit. One case settled, another ended in default, one remains active, and the final lawsuit was dropped after an apology from Jomha.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: In 2009, Washington removed a century-old dike and let tides reclaim 762 acres
item.description: In 2009, the decision to remove sea dikes from the Nisqually River Delta paved the way for a remarkable transformation, rejuvenating 762 acres of marshland. Young Chinook salmon swiftly adapted to the new tidal channels, fostering their feeding and growth. This comprehensive restoration successfully re-established 21 miles of ancestral tidal channels with Puget Sound, showcasing a promising blueprint for coastal resilience in the West Coast regions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2016, conservationists put the bends back into a Lake District river straightened 200 years earlier
item.description: Conservationists undertook an inspiring project to restore the natural meanders of Swindale Beck, which had been straightened for centuries. Within just a few months, the restored gravel beds welcomed back the Atlantic salmon to spawn, while also decreasing flood risks and enhancing drinking water quality for millions. This remarkable recovery fostered a thriving habitat for aquatic insects and river birds, ultimately earning the UK River Prize in 2022.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: MrBeast reacts as viral Terraria kid reveals heartbreaking reason behind pause in Terraria videos
item.description: In a heartfelt announcement, Instagram creator michaelshowscoolthings shared that he will be taking a break from his engaging Terraria content due to his family’s unexpected financial strains and an upcoming move. This tough personal ordeal has led him to reassess his priorities. MrBeast, the renowned YouTube star, reached out with uplifting words to help the young creator navigate through this challenging chapter.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 5 insane Twitch records that may be nearly impossible for another streamer to break
item.description: Twitch has seen some unbelievable milestones, but five records stand far above the rest. Ibai Llanos reached more than 9.3 million peak viewers, Kai Cenat crossed 1.1 million active subscribers, and Neuro-sama hit Level 126 on a Hype Train. TheGrefg’s Fortnite reveal reached 2.47 million viewers, while Ludwig’s month-long subathon created an endurance benchmark that remains extremely difficult to extend further.

item.title: Khamzat Chimaev accepts surprising fight offer from top UFC contender after losing middleweight title
item.description: In a bold move, Caio Borralho has issued a challenge to Khamzat Chimaev for a prospective fight, proposing two dates in November and December. After losing his middleweight title, Chimaev is weighing his options. This clash could play a pivotal role in shaping the future of the middleweight division, with Borralho ranked sixth and Chimaev ranked twelfth globally.

item.title: In 2020, Ohio removed a dam from the once-polluted Cuyahoga River; it reopened 39 km of habitat
item.description: The removal of the Brecksville Diversion Dam has enhanced river habitats, allowing migrating fish to thrive. Researchers documented the arrival of fifteen new fish species within the lower Cuyahoga River. While native species have successfully reestablished their presence, the advent of nonnative species also marked a significant change in the ecosystem. Ongoing efforts to eliminate more dams aim to further rejuvenate the Cuyahoga River basin for future generations.
